targetAudience.primary: Engineering leads, security architects, and governance owners designing AI-assisted approval flows
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands code review, policy gates, delegated agents, and auditable state transitions.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A positive AI judgment may be mistaken for authority to approve, or an old approval may remain effective after its target, policy, or authorization evidence changes.

whyNow: GitHub Copilot's documented review controls and OpenAI Codex's versioned Guardian authorization lifecycle expose the same governance boundary at organizational and agent-runtime layers.

externalHook.description: Two independent product layers distinguish a model's positive judgment from the policy and fresh evidence that make it operationally effective.

coreProposition: An AI approval judgment becomes an effective sign-off only when separately authorized for a named gate, scope, and freshness identity; changes to the reviewed object, governing evidence, or authority-sensitive context must invalidate or re-evaluate that authority.

originalValue.description: Decomposes approval into judgment, approval capability, effective gate authority, scope, and freshness identity, then maps invalidation across organizational review and delegated-agent context changes.

readerTakeaway: Represent recommendation, authority grant, gate satisfaction, scope, and freshness as distinct auditable facts; invalidate the authority when any governing identity changes.

supported: GitHub documents that Copilot review assessment, permission to submit approval, and effect on merge requirements are separate controls.
GitHub documents scope and freshness constraints, including policy hierarchy, optional path qualification, and dismissal after new commits.
The examined Codex maintainer implementation versions Guardian root-authorization evidence and cancels or strips stale or inherited approval in covered paths.
The comparison supports a bounded invariant that positive judgment is not self-authorizing and authority must have a checkable freshness identity.
unsupported: Proof of a legal or human principal identity
Equivalence between GitHub organizational policy and Codex runtime authorization
uncertain: Which harmless changes may preserve authority
How in-flight effects should be cancelled or reconciled when authority becomes stale

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article compares external public policy and open-source implementation evidence; no first-party project is needed for the argument.

decisionReason: The two distinct samples support an actionable governance model with explicit counterarguments and evidence boundaries without claiming protocol equivalence.
